body:
When using Jolt physics, it seems like the behavior also differs based on whether or not the soft body is sleeping.  The rendered object is incorrect in either case, but if the soft body was sleeping it does not get woken up so that physics apply to its new location.
For instance, if you click the "Raise Body" button in the MRP the body will fall downwards due to gravity if it was still awake, but if it had already settled into a sleeping state then it won't fall due to gravity after "Raise Body" is clicked.

Changing `JoltSoftBody3D::set_transform()` to also call `wake_up()` appears to fix that problem.

It looks like the bug is that `SoftBody3D` disables transform notifications when attempting to reset the transform:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e1b4101e3460dd9c6ba0b7f8d88e9751b8383f5b/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp#L383-L386

I believe the intent here is to prevent it from receiving notifications about its own change, and processing this in a loop.
However, this also causes the code in the parent `VisualInstance3D` class to be skipped, so the RenderingServer never gets told about the transform being reset to 0:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/e1b4101e3460dd9c6ba0b7f8d88e9751b8383f5b/scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp#L94

See https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/physics/thread/i9vYNaP4iuQYd427g .

As far as I can make out, `SoftBody` is using a nasty hack to set the transform, and it only works in the particular situation of setting the soft body up the first time (from the editor).

The `soft_body_set_transform()` API is currently acting as a relative API. If you call it twice, it will xform the softbody by that amount twice. If you think about it, setting the transform of a gloopy mess is a somewhat undefined operation (because you may get e.g. stray verts affecting centre of mass). The only highly "defined" operation probably is a relative xform, but that isn't easy to set up via the editor's regular systems, hence this hack I believe.

I cover some possible approaches in the chat there, like calculating a centre of mass and allowing an absolute `set_transform`. But currently the behaviour is crazy (and also broke the assumptions of #105901 ).

I prepared some fixes to softbody after #106863 (which caused some dubious changes to non-interpolated behaviour which I pointed out there), but I didn't make a PR in the end partly because I don't want to end up maintaining soft body (you touch it, you maintain it 😁 ).

I think rather than diving into PRs, we really need a proposal to agree on changing the behaviour of `SoftBody` to something sensible. It's possible it will have to be compat breaking (as the current behaviour is bonkers).

You were correct to mention `_set_use_identity_transform()` as a possibility, which I added a while back to handle some similar cases where global xforms were used in the visual server, it was much more sensible than the hacks previously used for some cases like particles, and was necessary for interpolation to work correctly. (`toplevel` is similarish concept, but they work slightly differently.)

> However, this also causes the code in the parent `VisualInstance3D` class to be skipped, so the RenderingServer never gets told about the transform being reset to 0:

I'm not sure the `RenderingServer` ever gets told about `instance` xforms, hence it is always at the origin. But `_set_use_identity_transform()` is usually a better way of achieving this (it was added _after_ `SoftBody`).

> I'm not sure the RenderingServer ever gets told about instance xforms

I'm pretty sure `VisualInstance3D` is telling the `RenderingServer` about the transform here

For SoftBody3D here, I believe what is happening is that:
1. User code updates the transform, causing the node to add itself to the SceneTree xform_change_list to be notified
2. The scene tree flushes notifications, and uses `Object::_notification_forwardv()` which will run `VisualInstance3D::_notification()` first, followed by `SoftBody3D::_notification()` second.
3. `VisualInstance3D` therefore runs first, informing the `RenderingServer` about the real requested transform change.
4. The `SoftBody3D` notification handler then runs, and resets the transform back to the identity.  However, it suppresses notifications for this, causing `VisualInstance3D` to never see the second update, and never reset the `RenderingServer` transform back to 0.


> As far as I can make out, SoftBody is using a nasty hack to set the transform

I agree that this is a wacky hack.  It appears to pre-date the existence of `_set_use_identity_transform()`, and I agree that updating it to use `_set_use_identity_transform()` would be a much nicer fix.


I have thoughts about how to make SoftBody3D have a somewhat sane and explainable behavior here.  I can go ahead and work on writing up a proposal.  At a high level:

1. I do agree that `SoftBody3D` should use `_set_use_identity_transform()` to always render at the origin, regardless of its transform.
2. I think that the SoftBody3D transform should only be used to specify the initial starting location of the mesh when it is first added to the scene and converted from its static geometry to a dynamic mesh.
3. If the transform is modified when a soft body is already in the scene, we apply the relative transform between the old and new global transform to the dynamic body.  (Alternatively, I'd also be okay if we simply ignored the change, and the new change only took effect the next time set_mesh() was called.  A bunch of other soft body properties like pressure, stiffness, etc, also only take effect when the mesh changes.)

Note that I think this behavior would make sense with my PhysicsServer3D API proposal at godotengine/godot-proposals#12670, where I am proposing we deprecate `PhysicsServer3D::soft_body_set_mesh()`, and replace it with a `soft_body_set_settings()` API that behaves a bit more like Jolt's `SoftBodySharedSettings` class.  With this API you can create many SoftBody3D instances using the same settings, having different initial transforms for different instances would allow them to be placed at different locations in the world.

With that said, I think SoftBody3D probably needs some other fixes before this can be one.  e.g., I think #108061 is important, because otherwise SoftBody3D goes through some slightly weird intermediate states between when the mesh is set and when it actually tells the physics server and then when it actually receives the first vertex updates and has correct mesh data in the right world transform.
